issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String (the saloon name), but the provided solution defines a no-argument constructor. Additionally, the example Main (in the template/solution) instantiates SealSaloon with no arguments, which conflicts with the textual requirement. This inconsistency will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and may cause tests or examples to disagree with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor (and document how the saloon name should be handled if needed), and keep examples that use new SealSaloon(); or (B) Change the example Main and the solution to call new SealSaloon("name") and implement a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor (optionally keep a no-arg constructor if examples/tests require it). Update the UML and all references accordingly.

issues.description: Ambiguity about the 'stock' attribute initialization and mutability: the problem text initially instructs to create a final Stock stock and initialize it in the SealSaloon constructor (implying an instance field initialized per-instance), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). Initializing a static stock in the constructor is incongruous. The solution declares a static final stock initialized at declaration. This mixed guidance (instance final initialized in constructor vs. static shared) is inconsistent and may confuse students where and how to declare/initialize stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and make consistent whether 'stock' is an instance field or a shared static field. If stock is intended to be shared across all SealSaloon instances, explicitly state it should be declared static (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock()) and remove the instruction to initialize it in the constructor. If it should be per-instance, remove the static requirement and keep initialization in the constructor. Update the problem statement examples and UML to reflect the chosen approach.
